what_broke: Read new int(5) as allocating an array of 5 ints, when it actually allocates one int initialized to the value 5. Confused parenthesis-initializer syntax (new T(x)) with bracket-array syntax (new T[x]).
source_hint: src/data/topics/cpp/dynamic-alloc.js — 'Allocating with new' card; src/data/topics/cpp/dynamic-arrays.js — 'Creating a dynamic array' card

what_broke: After delete a; where b held the same address as a, assumed cout << *b would still deterministically print the old value (10). Missed that delete does not null the pointer variables involved, and that reading through a dangling pointer is undefined behavior, not a guaranteed stale read.
